title: Nurmagomedov vs. Hughes 2: PFL Lightweight Title Rematch Date & Preview
text:
Nurmagomedov and Hughes Set for Explosive PFL Rematch in dubai The Professional Fighters League (PFL) is poised to deliver another thrilling lightweight showdown as Usman Nurmagomedov and Paul Hughes prepare to settle their score in a highly anticipated rematch on October 3rd in Dubai.The bout, the main event of PFL Champions Series 3, comes nine months after a contentious first encounter that many believe Hughes narrowly won.
A Fight for the Ages Their initial clash on January 25th in Dubai was widely hailed as a potential fight of the year contender. The undefeated Nurmagomedov edged out Hughes by majority decision, wiht judges’ scores of 47-47 and 48-46 (twice). However, the result remains a point of contention, fueling a bitter rivalry that has played out publicly in the months since.
Hughes Accuses PFL of Intervention The core of the animosity stems from Hughes’ firm belief that the PFL institution intervened to secure a second fight with Nurmagomedov. Speaking with BBC Sport NI,the 28-year-old Northern Ireland native asserted,”I’m certain he didn’t want this,he tried to delay this for the longest period,that’s why the fight only got done very recently.” Hughes continued, stating that Nurmagomedov was compelled to accept the rematch under threat of being stripped of his title.
Nurmagomedov Dismisses Claims,Promises Dominance Nurmagomedov,27,a Dagestan native and cousin of former UFC champion Khabib Nurmagomedov,dismissed Hughes’ accusations with a laugh during an interview with CBS Sports. He questioned whether Hughes would offer a rematch if the roles were reversed, stating, “If Paul Hughes, maybe in [his] next life, if he might potentially be in the same position where I am and he beat me, ask him if he is going to give me a chance again, or not?” Nurmagomedov confidently predicted a decisive victory, declaring, “I’m going to beat him twice. Nothing has changed. This guy is not on my level.”
A Tale of Two Styles The first fight revealed a compelling stylistic clash. Nurmagomedov initially dominated the first two rounds, showcasing his grappling prowess. However, as the fight progressed, fatigue appeared to set in, and Hughes began to mount a comeback with impactful body punches. The champion even appeared weary in the fourth round before an accidental head clash provided a brief respite.
Hughes believes he exposed vulnerabilities in Nurmagomedov’s conditioning and game plan. “I brought him into a fight that he hadn’t been in before, a true and proper fight,” Hughes told CBS Sports. He intends to capitalize on this in the rematch, promising relentless pressure. “I will break him at some point in this fight, no question,” Hughes stated. “I am going to make him scramble for his life for every single position and I am not going to get off of him until I have him broken.”
Nurmagomedov Acknowledges Mistakes, Vows Advancement Nurmagomedov conceded that he made errors in their first meeting, attributing them to a difficult training camp and a lack of respect for Hughes’ abilities. He maintains, however, that he is always humble in his approach to fighting and that Hughes’ success was due to his own strategic missteps. Despite this, his closing remarks were anything but humble, recalling Hughes’ emotional reaction to the first fight’s outcome. “When [Hughes] lost [the first] fight,he was crying,” Nurmagomedov said with a smirk. “A million people are watching and he cried. A man crying. I’m going to make him cry again.”
The rematch promises to be a captivating display of skill,will,and perhaps,a settling of a deeply personal score. With both fighters determined to prove their dominance, the PFL Champions Series 3 event is shaping up to be a must-see for MMA fans worldwide.
